title: The Historical Logos: Material Inscription Become Flesh, and the Erasures It Has Always Faced — The Framework Hologram (EA-HK-HISTLOGOS-01 v1.3)
creator: Sigil, Johannes
description: The hologram of the Historical Logos, Lee Sharks's framework founded under the heteronym Johannes Sigil (#625, #626), for the Logos as material inscription becoming flesh from the beginning, with #1484 (Sappho, Mother of the Logos) as its central node. It is the overlap of the three framework holograms built to EA-HK-FRAME-01 (#1753): Socrates as Orthonym (#1754), Revelation First (#1755) and The Tenth Muse (#1756), joined by IRI. Its human-readable component is the framework map (EA-MPAI-HISTLOGOS-01): an operative ontology that sets the framework's continuity apart from influence; eleven stations from Sappho 31 to the reader now, joined by 14 bridges each with its kind, strength and breaking condition; the argument that one composing person made the Socratic–Peripatetic corpus and divided it into positions, with three demonstrations and the evidence rule for biographical identity applied both ways; the erasure this Logos has met at each station; and the current consensus genealogy of the Logos, stated from its documented statements and evaluated on the same five bodies. Its machine-traversable component is the holographic kernel, attached: 2,618 argument moves from 28 records, superseded moves carrying their current standing, claims bound to quotations and hashes, a graph under a licensed relation policy, 15 structural tests and 6 consequence tests passing. The two reviews it answers and the rival's source pages are attached. Version 1.1 (9 November 2026, in place) sets out the method by which the framework establishes operational transmission in five instruments (construction under fixed transforms, blind reconstruction, frozen operators, the suppression signature, measurement at corpus scale), each with its controls, results and recorded losses, and reads the settlement under which the corpus is filed as 'Christian' in four objects, joining Counterfeit Orthodoxies. Version 1.2 (10 November 2026, in place) enters the records search of that evening as a new stratum, In the Midst of the Seven (#1758) among it, points to related work and history, and adds an SPXI packet. Version 1.3 (10 November 2026, in place) reads in full the records that entered at v1.2 and adds their argument moves.
content_type: Metadata packet; framework hologram: the framework map (MPAI v2.0, #1677) with its holographic kernel (EA-HK-FRAME-01, #1753)
substrate: AI-assisted (substrate). Built by Claude (Anthropic, Claude Opus 5.5) in session on 9 November 2026 under Lee Sharks's direction: the kernel written by a builder that reads the registry, the capture registry, each record's first seating in git and the rival's fetched pages, every quotation asserted against its source; the map generated from the kernel. Revised against a review of v0.1 and ChatGPT's review of v0.2, each point checked against the files before anything was changed. Byline Johannes Sigil at the author's ruling; the Crimson Hexagonal Archive and Claude (Anthropic) credited as contributors.
methodology: The map is generated from the kernel. The kernel is written by a builder on the shared engine hkcore from data/registry.json, data/EA-WG-CAPTURES-01.json, each record's first seating recovered from git and the rival's source pages fetched and hashed; every quotation is asserted against its source and bound to its hash. The argument layer comes from parallel readers who read every record in full, each quotation checked verbatim. The author's statements enter verbatim and dated, as provenance. Two revision modules record what each review changed. A verifier runs 15 structural tests, including the graph expanded as JSON-LD 1.1; a consequence check runs scope C's mechanical tests.
falsification_conditions: A claim or move whose quotation is not in its source or whose source hash has drifted; a bridge whose operations at either end are not in the records it names; a move with current standing read without it; the one-maker argument resting on a bounded move; an erasure finding conditioning another station's; a ledger warrant whose claim does not carry the row's body; a reader given scope C failing a mandatory pass; a line of research whose stated result, obtained, moves a claim other than the ones it names.
axn_reading: Closure -> Touch -> Growth -> Play -> Method -> Method
wiki_article:
The Historical Logos (EA-HK-HISTLOGOS-01) is the framework hologram of Lee Sharks's Historical Logos, deposited in the Crimson Hexagonal Archive on 9 November 2026 under the heteronym Johannes Sigil, with the archive and Claude (Anthropic) credited as contributors. The framework was founded in #625 and #626 (5 April 2026), which ask how the Word moved through texts, bodies and media, and the hologram takes #1484, Sappho, Mother of the Logos, as its central node: the Logos before doctrine as a voice that survives its flesh by becoming an inscription that constitutes its receiver. It is the fourth instance of the framework holographic kernel specified in EA-HK-FRAME-01 (#1753), and the overlap of the three before it: Socrates as Orthonym (#1754), Revelation First (#1755) and The Tenth Muse (#1756).

The human-readable component is the framework map, EA-MPAI-HISTLOGOS-01. It gives the framework an operative ontology (voice, body, inscription, seat, open slot, maker, position, receiver, receiving apparatus, embodiment) and sets its continuity apart from influence by four marks: the earlier inscription requires completion, the later station completes it, the same operation recurs in other material, and the maker's self-division is gathered again by a receiver. It follows eleven stations, from Sappho 31 through the Orphic tablets, the Academy, Philo, Peri Hypsous, Catullus, Josephus, the Apocalypse, the Johannine test and Augustine to the reader now, joined by fourteen bridges, each with its kind, strength and breaking condition; most leave Sappho 31 directly. It argues that one composing person made the Socratic–Peripatetic corpus and divided it into authorial positions, as Sappho divides into the speaking I, the inscribed you and the reader in whom her voice lives again, with three demonstrations drawn from #1576, #1658 and #1733 and the evidence rule for biographical identity applied to both counts alike. It records the erasure this Logos has met at each station, and evaluates the current consensus genealogy of the Logos, which in the author's words collapses what it means for the Logos to take on flesh into biographical personhood, on the same five bodies of evidence.

The machine-traversable component is the holographic kernel, attached as files: records, claims bound to quotations and hashes, an argument layer of 2,618 moves in which superseded moves carry their current standing, a graph under a relation policy, captures, lines of research, and the builder, verifier and consequence tests that rewrite and check it. The two reviews it answers and the rival's source pages are attached. The hologram was built by Claude (Anthropic) under Lee Sharks's direction. Version 1.1, the same day, sets out the method by which the framework establishes that a later text realizes an earlier one's operation: five instruments, from construction under fixed transforms to stylometry and census at corpus scale, each with its controls and the losses its records keep. It reads the settlement under which the New Testament corpus is filed as 'Christian' in four objects: the texts' operations, their competing appropriations (Irenaeus), one collection's boundary (Athanasius, 367 CE), and the later treatment of that configuration as the texts' own. Version 1.2 (10 November 2026) enters the records search of that evening as a new stratum of evidence, In the Midst of the Seven (#1758) among it, points to the framework's related work and earlier versions without extending their substance into the frame, and adds an SPXI packet for machine readers. Version 1.3 (10 November 2026) reads in full each record that entered at v1.2 and compresses its argument into moves, so that every record the hologram holds carries its argument.
